general.title: Why Naive Text Extraction Destroys RAG on Multi-Column PDFs (and How to Fix Reading Order)
general.describe: When an AI retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline hallucinates on a question sourced from a scientific paper or financial report, the debugging process almost invariably looks at the wrong layer. Engineers test alternative embedding models, tweak chunk token budgets, or introduce expensive cross-encoder rerankers. Yet in a surprising fraction of failure cases, the corruption happens before embedding: in the text extraction layer where the parser attempts to reconstruct human reading order from a format that was never designed to store it. general.title: Boundary change, not version bump
general.describe: The WASI Subgroup voted to ratify WASI 0.3.0, and the change sitting under the version number is that stream<T> , future<T> , and async are now first-class constructs in the WebAssembly Component Model's canonical ABI. The host owns a single event loop, shared by every component it runs, and the runtime does the scheduling. That reframes what a WASI version means here. In 0.2 each component carried its own event loop and async runtime. A single component could run on a host, but two of those loops had no way to coordinate.
